  <entry>
    <id>http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.36497v1</id>
    <title>Failure of the congruence Hasse principle for commutators in orientable surface groups</title>
    <updated>2026-10-27T01:54:38Z</updated>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.36497v1" rel="alternate" type="text/html"/>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.36497v1" rel="related" type="application/pdf" title="pdf"/>
    <summary>Ghosh, Meiri and Sarnak showed that the commutator equation over $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$ satisfies a profinite local to global principle, and that for a prime $\ell\equiv\pm1$ mod $5$ it fails for $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z}[1/\ell])$ with a reciprocity obstruction. We extend the failure to surface groups. For the genus-$2$ surface group $Γ_2$ we construct an explicit representation $ρ:Γ_2\to\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathcal{O}_{K,S})$, where $K=\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{5})$ and $\mathcal{O}_{K,S}=\mathbb{Z}[\frac{1+\sqrt{5}}{2},\frac{1}{10}]$, whose quotients modulo the maximal ideals are the full groups $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{F}_q)$ except in residue characteristic $3$, where the quotient has order $24$. For every $k\ge2$ the word $[a_1,b_1]^k$ is not a commutator in $Γ_2$, while its image is a commutator in every one of these quotients. The same holds for every surface group $Γ_g$ with $g\ge2$.</summary>
    <category term="math.GR" scheme="http://arxiv.org/schemas/atom"/>
    <category term="math.NT" scheme="http://arxiv.org/schemas/atom"/>

  <entry>
    <id>http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.36401v1</id>
    <title>Degree-one cohomology of metacyclic $2$-groups: a low-bit dichotomy</title>
    <updated>2026-10-26T23:29:58Z</updated>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.36401v1" rel="alternate" type="text/html"/>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.36401v1" rel="related" type="application/pdf" title="pdf"/>
    <summary>We study the subalgebra generated by degree-one mod-$2$ cohomology for metacyclic $2$-groups $G=\langle a,b\mid a^{2^α}=1,\ b^{2^m}=a^c,\ b^{-1}ab=a^r\rangle$ with unique normal forms, where $α,m\ge2$ and $r\equiv-1\pmod4$. Presentation compatibility forces $c=0$ or $2^{α-1}$ and $G^{\mathrm{ab}}\cong C_2\times C_{2^m}$. If $c\equiv0\pmod4$, the degree-one-generated algebra is $\mathbb{F}_2 [x,y]/(y^2,x^2+xy)$, a four-dimensional algebra shared by the four nonmodular types of Aaboun--Zekhnini. The unique exceptional case $α=2$, $c=2$ is modular and has infinite-dimensional degree-one algebra $\mathbb{F}_2[x,y]/(y^2,x^2y)$. The regular algebra is PBW, Koszul, universally Koszul, and strongly Koszul, whereas the modular algebra is not Koszul. We realize the regular algebra by inflation from the common quotient $C_4\rtimes_{-1}C_4$ and identify its quadratic dual with the characteristic-two Jordan plane. For the inversion tower $C_4\rtimes_{-1}C_{2^m}$, we give uniform presentations of the full mod-$2$ cohomology rings and determine the kernels and images of inflation in every degree. Their direct limit yields the continuous cohomology ring of $C_4\rtimes_{-1}\mathbb Z_2$. We also record an arithmetic consequence for Galois groups arising over cyclotomic $\mathbb Z_2$-extensions of real quadratic fields.</summary>
    <category term="math.GR" scheme="http://arxiv.org/schemas/atom"/>
    <category term="math.RA" scheme="http://arxiv.org/schemas/atom"/>
    <published>2026-10-26T23:29:58Z</published>
    <arxiv:primary_category term="math.GR"/>
    <author>
      <name>Marina Palaisti</name>
    </author>
  </entry>
  <entry>
    <id>http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.36394v1</id>
    <title>Realizing graph automorphisms as geometric symmetries of straight line drawings</title>
    <updated>2026-10-26T23:19:27Z</updated>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.36394v1" rel="alternate" type="text/html"/>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.36394v1" rel="related" type="application/pdf" title="pdf"/>
    <summary>Given a finite graph $G$, we characterize the automorphisms and automorphism groups of $G$ that can be realized as geometric symmetries and symmetry groups of straight line drawings of $G$ in the plane. In doing so, we correct a previous version of this characterization from the literature. As an application, we show that the graphs recently constructed by the first two authors to disprove the Polycirculant Conjecture, which have orders $16{,}464^k$ for each positive integer $k$, are the first known vertex-transitive graphs with no non-trivial realizable geometric symmetries. We also construct infinite families of graphs that exhibit all possible kinds of geometric symmetry.</summary>

  <entry>
    <id>http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.36302v1</id>
    <title>The Andreadakis conjecture</title>
    <updated>2026-10-26T21:27:15Z</updated>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.36302v1" rel="alternate" type="text/html"/>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.36302v1" rel="related" type="application/pdf" title="pdf"/>
    <summary>For $n\ge2$, let $F_n$ be the free group of rank $n$, and let $\IA(F_n)$ be the group of automorphisms of $F_n$ acting trivially on its abelianization. Two natural filtrations of $\IA(F_n)$ are its lower central series $γ_c(\IA(F_n))$ and the Andreadakis filtration $\mathrm{I}_{c+1}\mathrm{A}(F_n)$, consisting of automorphisms acting trivially on $F_n/γ_{c+1}(F_n)$, $c \geq 1$. Andreadakis conjectured that these filtrations coincide. We disprove this conjecture for every $n\ge3$ and $c\ge4$.</summary>
    <category term="math.GR" scheme="http://arxiv.org/schemas/atom"/>
    <published>2026-10-26T21:27:15Z</published>

    <id>http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.36259v1</id>
    <title>Filling knots and essential geodesic systole</title>
    <updated>2026-10-26T20:37:10Z</updated>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.36259v1" rel="alternate" type="text/html"/>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.36259v1" rel="related" type="application/pdf" title="pdf"/>
    <summary>We prove that every closed, orientable $3$--manifold contains hyperbolic knots with arbitrarily large essential geodesic systole. That is, for any $3$--manifold $M$, and $R> 0$ there is a hyperbolic knot $K \subset M$ such that every closed geodesic in the knot complement which is non-null-homotopic in $M$ has length at least $R$. The construction also produces filling knots, in the sense of Freedman-Krushkal [FreeKrus2023]. This answers two questions of Biringer.</summary>

    <id>http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.36211v1</id>
    <title>Recognizing convergence actions as proper isometric actions on hyperbolic spaces</title>
    <updated>2026-10-26T19:44:33Z</updated>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.36211v1" rel="alternate" type="text/html"/>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.36211v1" rel="related" type="application/pdf" title="pdf"/>
    <summary>Relying merely on B.I. (a.k.a. Bowditch's intelligence), we show that whenever a group $G$ admits a convergence action on a compact perfect metrizable space $M$, there is a hyperbolic space $X$ along with a proper isometric action of $G$ on $X$ inducing a $G$-equivariant homeomorphism $f:M \rightarrow \partial X.$ This answers a question by Misha Kapovich.</summary>

    <id>http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.36165v1</id>
    <title>A new infinite family of covers of complete graphs that admit a half-transitive action of a Suzuki simple group</title>
    <updated>2026-10-26T19:00:40Z</updated>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.36165v1" rel="alternate" type="text/html"/>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.36165v1" rel="related" type="application/pdf" title="pdf"/>
    <summary>We construct a new infinite family of antipodal $2(q-1)$-covers of complete graphs $K_{q^2+1}$ of diameter $3$, where $q=2^{2e+1}\ge 8$, admitting a half-transitive action of the Suzuki simple group $Sz(q)$. We further show that each constructed cover admits an involutory automorphism interchanging the two $Sz(q)$-orbits on arcs, which yields that its full automorphism group is arc-transitive.</summary>
    <category term="math.CO" scheme="http://arxiv.org/schemas/atom"/>
    <category term="math.GR" scheme="http://arxiv.org/schemas/atom"/>

  <entry>
    <id>http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.35841v1</id>
    <title>Infranormal Kazhdan subgroups and instability in finite actions</title>
    <updated>2026-10-26T17:54:16Z</updated>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.35841v1" rel="alternate" type="text/html"/>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.35841v1" rel="related" type="application/pdf" title="pdf"/>
    <summary>We prove that the group $G=\mathbb{Z}[1/2]^3\rtimes(\operatorname{SL}_3(\mathbb{Z})\times\mathbb{Z})$ is finitely presented and residually finite, but is not stable in finite actions, answering a question of Gohla and Thom. The proof uses the infranormal Kazhdan subgroup $H=\mathbb{Z}^3\rtimes\operatorname{SL}_3(\mathbb{Z})$ and its normal closure $N$ in $G$. A Kazhdan projection estimate shows that, in any $G$-action weakly contained in finite actions, every $H$-invariant measurable subset is also $N$-invariant. We construct an explicit sofic approximation of $G$ whose limit action contains a measurable subset that is $H$-invariant but not $N$-invariant.</summary>
    <category term="math.GR" scheme="http://arxiv.org/schemas/atom"/>
    <published>2026-10-26T17:54:16Z</published>
    <arxiv:comment>10 pages</arxiv:comment>

      <name>Jonas Pinke</name>

    <id>http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.35674v1</id>
    <title>Projections in reduced group C*-algebras with prescribed trace values in (0,1)</title>
    <updated>2026-10-26T16:16:19Z</updated>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.35674v1" rel="alternate" type="text/html"/>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.35674v1" rel="related" type="application/pdf" title="pdf"/>
    <summary>Building on OpenAI's preprint, we construct, for every real number $r\in(0,1)$, a finitely generated discrete group $G_r$ and a projection $e_r\in C_r^*(G_r)$ whose canonical trace is $r$. The construction encodes the geometry of expanders in the dynamics of a semidirect product of groups. For irrational $r$, the $K$-theory class $[e_r]$ is not in the image of the reduced Baum--Connes map. The groups $G_r$ have torsion and satisfy the maximal strong Novikov conjecture.</summary>
    <category term="math.OA" scheme="http://arxiv.org/schemas/atom"/>
    <category term="math.GR" scheme="http://arxiv.org/schemas/atom"/>

    </author>

  <entry>
    <id>http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.35643v1</id>
    <title>Finite groups with exactly 2p + 1 subgroups of order p</title>
    <updated>2026-10-26T15:52:18Z</updated>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.35643v1" rel="alternate" type="text/html"/>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.35643v1" rel="related" type="application/pdf" title="pdf"/>
    <summary>Let m_p(G) be the number of elements of order p in a finite group G, p prime. We prove that there is no finite simple group G with m_p(G) = 2p^2-p-1, and that a finite group with this property exists if and only if 2p+1 is prime or 3^f with f an odd prime. This concerns an open problem and extends the classification of finite groups with few elements of prime order.</summary>
    <category term="math.GR" scheme="http://arxiv.org/schemas/atom"/>
    <published>2026-10-26T15:52:18Z</published>
